(c) Living in Emergency Hospitals.

No. of hospitals      :       12
No. of patients       :       1,024

As compared with statistics made on November 2,
the number of refugees housed in camps show a decrease
from 52,666 to 50,574, the number of refugees living in
alleyways and vacant houses (not camps) show an increase
from 6,920 to 7,790 and the number of refugee patients
in emergency hospitals has decreased from 1,034 to 1,024.

Revised lists of (a) refugee camps together with
their present accommodation, (b) number of refugees living
in alleyways and vacant houses and (c) emergency hospitals
for refugees together with their accommodation are attached
as appendices "A", "B" and "C" respectively.

During the month of November, the work on the
removal of refugee camps from the down-town area and the
subsequent accommodation in other camps in the Western Dis-
trict has been continued by the Federation of Charity Organi-
zations, 35 Yunnan Road, and the Shanghai Emergency Relief
Committee, 1454 Avenue Edward VII. (this Committee wound up
its affairs and handed over to the Shanghai Refugee Relief
Association, 93 Canton Road at the end of October, 1938 (
Vide Intelligence Report dated November 1, 1938)).

Those camps which were formerly under the direct
charge of the Cantonese Fellow Countrymen's Association,
have been placed under the charge of the Federation of Charity
Organizations, 35 Yunnan Road, as from November, 1938.

与11月2日的统计数据相比，安置在难民营的难民人数从52,666人减少至50,574人，居住在里弄和空屋（非难民营）的难民人数从6,920人增加至7,790人，应急医院中的难民病患人数从1,034人减少至1,024人。

11月份期间，慈善团体联合会（云南路35号）和上海急赈会（爱德华七世路1454号）继续开展将市中心区域的难民营迁出并随后安置在西区其他难民营的工作。（该委员会于1938年10月底结束事务并移交给上海难民救济协会，广东路93号（参见1938年11月1日的情报报告））。

自1938年11月起，原由广东同乡会直接管理的难民营已移交由慈善团体联合会（云南路35号）管理。

- 2 -

(c) Living in Emergency Hospitals.
No. of hospitals : 12
No. of patients : 1,034

As compared with statistics made on October 3,
the number of refugees housed in camps show a decrease
from 61,240 to 52,666, the number of refugees living in
alleyways and vacant houses (not camps) from 7,099 to 6,920
and the number of refugee patients in emergency hospitals
from 1,224 to 1,034.

Revised lists of (a) refugee camps together with
their present accommodation, (b) number of refugees living
in alleyways and vacant houses and (c) emergency hospitals
for refugees together with their accommodation are attached
as appendices "A" "B" and "C" respectively.

With a view to increasing the working efficiency
of refugee relief, the Shanghai Emergency Relief Committee,
with offices in the Pootung Guild Building, 1454 Avenue
Edward VII, has during the month of October, erected twenty
huts on a piece of vacant ground next to premises No. 314,
Yenping Road, north of Connaught Road (Gordon Road District),
which is known as the Yenping Road Experimental Camp of the
Shanghai Emergency Relief Committee (上海難民救濟分會
延平路實驗收容所). Of the twenty huts, five are
utilized as offices for the camp staff, i.e. kitchens,
latrines and hot water shops, etc., while the remainder
accommodate refugees exclusively, there being space for
approximately 5,000.

为了提高难民救济的工作效率，上海急赈会（办事处设在爱多亚路1454号浦东会馆大楼）于十月期间，在康纳路（戈登路区）以北延平路314号旁的一块空地上，搭建了二十间棚屋，该地被称为上海急赈会延平路实验收容所（上海難民救濟分會 延平路實驗收容所）。在这二十间棚屋中，五间用作营地工作人员的办公室，即厨房、厕所和热水供应处等，其余部分专门用于安置难民，可容纳约5,000人。

- 4 -

For purposes of better control and efficient
management in internal organization, a scheme has been put
into operation whereby every sixteen refugees will form
themselves into a group with a Chief elected from amongst
themselves and he is responsible for the supervision and
control of the refugees in this group; every ten groups form
a Section with a Sectional Chief in charge; every two or three
Sections make a Room, with a Chief and a Deputy Chief in
charge, and they are directly responsible for the conduct of
all refugees under their charge.

The prevention of disease and other matters apper-
taining to sanitary projects and maintenance of hygienic
conditions in the Camp will be supervised by members of the
Public Health Department of the S.M.C. Arrangements for
the education of these refugees are being undertaken by Mr.
H.C. Chen (陳鶴琴), Chinese Education Officer of the
S.M.C., with a view to making the refugees support themselves.

Six huts similar to those of the Experimental Camp
have also been constructed by the Federation of Charity Organi-
zations, 35 Yunnan Road, on Yenping Road, south of Connaught
Road, known as the Yenping Camp of the Federation of Charity
Organizations (慈聯救災会延平收容所), with space
available for the accommodation of approximately 1,500 refugees.
Since its establishment 1,348 refugees have been removed
there from various camps under the charge of the Federation.
The Director and Vice-Directors of this Camp are Messrs. Tsang
Nai-zung (張乃仁), Ching Huh-fee (慶赫非) and Tseng
Kuo-chun (曾國) respectively.

为了更好地控制和有效管理内部组织，实施了一项方案，即每十六名难民组成一个小组，由组员选举一名组长，负责监督和管理本组难民；每十个小组组成一个区，由区长负责；每两或三个区组成一个室，由主任和副主任负责，他们直接对其管辖下所有难民的行为负责。

疾病预防及其他有关卫生项目和维持收容所卫生条件的工作，将由工部局公共卫生处成员进行监督。这些难民的教育安排正由工部局华务教育官陈鹤琴 (Mr. H.C. Chen) 负责进行，旨在使难民能够自食其力。

慈善团体联合会（云南路35号）也在康纳路以南的延平路上建造了六间与实验收容所类似的棚屋，称为慈善团体联合会延平收容所（慈聯救災会延平收容所），可容纳约1,500名难民。自成立以來，已有1,348名难民从慈善团体联合会管辖的各个收容所迁移至此。该收容所的主任和副主任分别为张乃仁 (Tsang Nai-zung)、庆赫非 (Ching Huh-fee) 和曾国 (Tseng Kuo-chun) 先生。

(c) Living in Emergency Hospitals.
No. of hospitals : 12

As compared with statistics made on September 1,
the number of refugees housed in camps has been decreased
from 63,574 to 61,240, the number of refugees living in
alleyways and vacant houses (not camps) has been decreased
from 7,404 to 7,099 and the number of refugee patients in
emergency hospitals decreased from 1,274 to 1,224.
Revised lists of (a) refugee camps together with
their present accommodation, (b) number of refugees living
in alleyways and vacant houses and (c) emergency hospitals
of refugees together with their accommodation are attached
as appendices "A" "B" and "C" respectively.
The sudden decrease in the total number of des-
titute refugees in the Settlement is due to the transfer
on September 24, 1938, of the refugees in the 3rd Refugee
Camp of the International Relief Committee on Luzon Road
(Chengtu Road District), numbering 558, to the 2nd Refugee
Camp on Route Herve de Sieyes, French Concession as the
owner of the property at Luzon Road desired to regain
possession of his property. Another factor may be
attributed to (1) refugees returning to their native homes,
(2) the obtaining of employment or funds to act as hawkers
and being able to remove, (3) dissatisfaction with the
limited amount and the unsavoury nature of the food supplied
in the camps.
During the month of September, the Refugee Re-

patriation Committee of the International Red Cross, Sun
Building, 505 Honan Road, repatriated 102 refugees to their
native places through Wenchow and Hongkong. The
repatriation of refugees by way of Canton, however, ceased on
20-9-38, upon receipt of a telegram from General Wu Te-chen,
Chairman of the Kwangtung Provincial Government, in which
the inadvisability of the step was explained.
Owing to financial difficulties, the Federation
of Charity Organizations, 35 Yunnan Road, terminated the
services of 38 staff members on 15-9-38, each member re-
ceiving a sum equivalent to two and a half months locomotion
allowance.
In response to a telegraphic appeal from the various
benevolent societies in Shanghai for funds, Mr. Hsu Shih-ying
(許世英), Chairman of the Refugee Relief Committee of
the National Government in Hankow, remitted from Hongkong
the sum of $50,000, which was received for distribution on
27-9-38 by the Federation of Charity Organizations.

c) Living in Emergency Hospitals.
No. of hospitals: 11
No. of patients: 1,344

As compared with statistics made on July 4, the number
of refugees housed in camps has been decreased from 68,316
to 66,486 but the number of refugees living in alleyways
and vacant houses has been increased from 6,310 to 6,516
and the number of refugee patients in emergency hospitals
increased from 1,339 to 1,344.

Revised lists of (a) refugee camps together with their
present accommodation, (b) number of refugees living in
alleyways and vacant houses and (c) emergency hospitals of
refugees together with their accommodation are attached as
appendices "A," "B" and "C" respectively.

pages.en:
REFUGEES ARRIVING IN SHANGHAI FROM HANKOW

After the fall of Shanghai
many Chinese fled to Hankow and to other parts in the
interior. They are now reported to be coming back
to Shanghai from Hankow as the fall of Hankow is imminent.
During the past few days, steamers arriving here from
Wenchow brought about 10,000 Chinese from Hankow; most
of them are wealthy people.
pages.zh:
从汉口抵达上海的难民

上海沦陷后，许多中国人逃往汉口及内地其他地区。据报，由于汉口即将沦陷，他们正从汉口返回上海。在过去几天里，从温州抵达此处的轮船带来了约10,000名来自汉口的中国人；其中大多数是富人。

    As compared with statistics made on June 6, the
number of camps has been reduced from 114 to 112, the
number of refugees housed in camps has been decreased
from 73,810 to 69,674, but the number of refugees living
in alleyways and vacant houses has been increased from
5,245 to 6,216, and the number of refugee patients in
emergency hospitals has been decreased from 1,448 to 1,330.
    Revised lists of (a) refugee camps together with
their present accommodation, (b) number of refugees living
in alleyways and vacant houses and (c) emergency hospitals
of refugees together with their accommodation are attached
as appendices "A", "B", and "C" respectively.

    Under the auspices of the management of the Dau
Yuan Refugee Camp of the Federation of Charity Organizations
situated in the Cemetery ground on North Chekiang Road,
the refugees accommodated in the above camp, numbering
4,321, recently inaugurated a mutual aid association.
The new organization has for its aim the promotion of
recreation and the procuring of employment for the
refugees accommodated therein.

S.I, Special Branch L. REGISTER
B. D...
REPORT
Date June 6, 1938.

Subject Refugees in the Settlement - present situation.

Made W/ and Forwarded by D.I. Crawford

There are approximately 80,503 destitute refugees living
in the Settlement. The number when compared with that report-
ed on May 18 has been reduced by 4002. The decrease is
attributable to (1) the reduction in the number of camps and
(2) the prevailing hot weather. Many of those refugees
have left their camps either for their native homes in places
around Shanghai or to stay with their relatives and friends
in this city.

Up-to-date statistics of refugees classified according
to police districts and divided into three headings, namely
(1) living in refugee camps, (2) living in alleyways and
vacant houses, and (3) living in emergency hospitals, are
given hereunder:-

报告
日期：1938年6月6日。

主题：租界内的难民 - 现状。

由警司克劳福德（Crawford）编制并呈报

租界内目前约有80,503名贫困难民居住。与5月18日报告的数据相比，人数减少了4002人。减少的原因在于：(1) 难民营数量的减少，以及 (2) 当前炎热的天气。许多难民已离开难民营，要么返回上海周边地区的原籍，要么投奔在本市的亲友。

No. of hospitals: 12

====
As compared with statistics made on May 18, the number
of camps has been reduced from 122 to 114, the number of
refugees housed in camps has been decreased from 77876 to
73810, the number of refugees living in alleyways and vacant
houses has been decreased from 5266 to 5245 but the number
of refugees in emergency hospitals has been increased from
1363 to 1448.
Revised lists of (a) refugee camps together with their
present accommodation, (b) number of refugees living in
alleyways and vacant houses and (c) emergency hospitals of
refugees together with their accommodation are attached as
appendices "A", "B" and "C" respectively.
C. Crawford

Subject Refugees in the Settlement. - Present Situation.
Made by and Forwarded by D. I. Crawford.

It is estimated that there are 84,505 destitute

As compared with the statistics made on April 30,
the number of camps has been reduced from 130 to 122, the
number of refugees housed in camps has been reduced from
78,310 to 77,876, the number of refugees living in alleyways
and vacant houses has been increased from 5,014 to 5,266,
while the number of refugees in emergency hospitals has been
increased from 1,216 to 1,363.

Revised lists of (a) refugee camps together with
their present accommodation, (b) number of refugees living in
alleyways and vacant houses, and (c) emergency hospitals for
refugees together with their accommodation, are attached as
Appendices "A", "B" and "C" respectively.
